Agility confirms early exploration of wheeled robots

Jonathan Hurst says the Digit developer is studying additional form factors. The wheeled design remains exploratory, with no product or launch date confirmed.

The Robot Report ↗25 September 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 1Videos 1

A new confirmation after the Digit 5 video

The Robot Report asked Jonathan Hurst about a wheeled robot rendering near the end of the Digit 5 launch video. His email confirmed that Agility is exploring several designs, including wheels. The new development is that confirmation, rather than another announcement of Digit 5.

Matching the form to the environment

Hurst said alternative approaches could bring robots to more environments sooner. The report contrasts wheels’ suitability for predictable, flat surfaces with the usefulness of legs around stairs, obstacles and uneven terrain.

No product definition yet

Asked whether this would be a wheeled Digit or a differently named and shaped robot, Hurst said it was too early to say and the work was just starting. Specifications, payload, reach, pricing and a market launch have not been confirmed.

A rendering is not a deployed prototype

The illustration comes from the existing launch video. It does not establish that a commercially ready wheeled prototype exists. Target tasks, physical testing and a decision to turn the exploration into a product remain developments to watch.
